what: Eat a mix of vegetables and fruit across the day (e.g., vegetables at lunch and dinner, fruit as a snack).
dose: At least 400 g of fruits and vegetables per day (WHO, everyone older than 10).
why: WHO lists this as a core component of a healthy diet for preventing noncommunicable diseases.

sources.title: WHO fact sheet: Healthy diet (updated 26 Jan 2026)
WHO updates guidelines on fats and carbohydrates

cue_suggestion: When plating lunch and dinner: vegetables go on the plate first.
minimum_version: One piece of fruit or one handful of vegetables today.
normal_version: Vegetables with two meals plus 1-2 fruit portions.
bonus_version: Try one new vegetable or seasonal fruit this week.
joy_pairing: Keep a 'fruit of the week' novelty pick; make a colourful salad bowl you photograph for a personal food journal.
friction_down: Pre-wash/cut vegetables after grocery day; keep a fruit bowl at eye level.
friction_up_for_competing: Store sweets in an opaque box on a high shelf.
if_then_plan: If I open the fridge for a snack, then I will take a fruit or cut vegetables first.
safety_or_stop_rule: None specific; wash produce well.
notes: Saudi Healthy Food Palm key message: 'Consume a variety of fruits and vegetables'.

name_en: Fibre from whole grains and pulses
what: Choose whole grains (brown bread, oats, brown rice, bulgur) and add pulses (lentils, beans, chickpeas, foul) to meals.
dose: At least 25 g/day of naturally occurring dietary fibre (WHO). Meta-analysis: greatest risk reduction at 25-29 g/day.
why: Higher fibre and whole-grain intakes are associated with lower mortality, coronary heart disease, stroke, type 2 diabetes and colorectal cancer; trials show lower bodyweight, blood pressure and cholesterol.

sources.title: WHO fact sheet: Healthy diet (updated 26 Jan 2026)
WHO updates guidelines on fats and carbohydrates
Carbohydrate quality and human health: a series of systematic reviews and meta-analyses (Lancet)
FAO FBDG record: Dietary guidelines for Saudis - the Healthy Food Palm (Saudi MOH)

cue_suggestion: At breakfast and when choosing the carbohydrate for lunch.
minimum_version: Swap one refined grain for a whole grain today.
normal_version: Whole grain at 2 meals + pulses in at least one meal.
bonus_version: Batch-cook a pot of lentil soup or chickpea salad for 3 days.
joy_pairing: Rotate cuisines: foul, adas soup, hummus bowls, overnight oats with fruit.
friction_down: Put whole-grain versions on the standing grocery list; keep canned chickpeas/beans in the pantry.
friction_up_for_competing: Don't restock white bread by default.
if_then_plan: If I make rice or bread, then I will choose the whole-grain version.
progression: self-paced; increase gradually to limit bloating (general practice, not source-specified).
safety_or_stop_rule: Increase fibre gradually and drink water; persistent GI symptoms -> see a doctor.
notes: Saudi Healthy Food Palm: 'Choose whole grains'.

what: Make water the default drink; replace soft drinks, sweetened juices, and sweetened coffee/tea drinks with water or unsweetened options.
dose: Not specified by source as a drink count; free sugars overall <10% of daily energy (WHO).
why: CDC links frequent sugary-drink intake to weight gain, obesity, type 2 diabetes, heart disease, cavities and gout; WHO notes even unsweetened fruit juices contain significant free sugars.

sources.title: CDC: Rethink Your Drink (page accessed 2026-09-28; year = access year)
WHO fact sheet: Healthy diet (updated 26 Jan 2026)
FAO FBDG record: Dietary guidelines for Saudis - the Healthy Food Palm (Saudi MOH)

cue_suggestion: Every time I sit at the desk / get in the car: water bottle in hand.
minimum_version: Replace one sugary drink today with water.
normal_version: Water with all meals; sugary drinks are an occasional planned treat, not a default.
bonus_version: Make a jug of infused water (lemon, cucumber, mint) for the day.
joy_pairing: A water bottle you love; infused water flavours (CDC suggests berries, lime, lemon, cucumber).
friction_down: Carry a reusable bottle and refill it (CDC tip); keep cold water ready in the fridge.
friction_up_for_competing: Don't keep soft drinks in the home fridge; remove saved delivery-app drink orders.
if_then_plan: If I crave a soft drink, then I will first drink a glass of cold water with lemon.
safety_or_stop_rule: None specific.
notes: General hydration targets are covered in the BODY cluster; this action is the nutrition swap only. Saudi Healthy Food Palm: 'Drink water'.

what: Limit added sugars and sweets (desserts, sweetened snacks, honey/syrups, juices) to planned, enjoyable portions.
dose: Free sugars <10% of total daily energy; limiting to 5% or less may give additional benefits (WHO).
why: WHO recommends limiting free sugars as part of a healthy diet to prevent unhealthy weight gain and NCDs.

sources.title: WHO fact sheet: Healthy diet (updated 26 Jan 2026)

cue_suggestion: After lunch (typical dessert moment) and at the evening gathering.
minimum_version: Choose the smaller portion of dessert today.
normal_version: Sweets are planned (e.g., weekend or family gathering) rather than automatic daily.
bonus_version: Try a fruit-based dessert (dates in moderation, fruit with yoghurt).
joy_pairing: Savour a planned treat slowly without screens so it's genuinely enjoyed.
friction_down: Buy small single portions instead of family packs.
friction_up_for_competing: Keep sweets out of sight (opaque tin, high shelf).
if_then_plan: If sweets are offered and I didn't plan one, then I will take a small piece and eat it slowly.
safety_or_stop_rule: Avoid 'forbidden food' rules; if restriction leads to preoccupation or bingeing, stop and speak with a professional.
notes: Percent-of-energy targets are for reference, not for daily calculation.

name_en: Less salt when cooking and eating
what: Reduce salt and high-sodium condiments when cooking, keep salt/salty sauces off the table, and limit salty snacks.
dose: Adults: less than 5 g salt per day (2 g sodium) (WHO).
why: WHO recommends limiting salt intake as part of a healthy diet (salt reduction lowers blood pressure risk).

sources.title: WHO fact sheet: Healthy diet (updated 26 Jan 2026)
FAO FBDG record: Dietary guidelines for Saudis - the Healthy Food Palm (Saudi MOH)

cue_suggestion: When cooking or setting the table.
minimum_version: Taste before salting today.
normal_version: Cook with herbs, lemon, spices; no salt shaker on the table.
bonus_version: Compare sodium on labels of 2 products you buy often and switch to the lower one.
joy_pairing: Build a spice kit (cumin, sumac, za'atar, lemon zest) and try a new blend weekly.
friction_down: Keep spices next to the stove, salt in a cupboard.
friction_up_for_competing: Buy salty snacks only in small packs.
if_then_plan: If a dish tastes bland, then I will add lemon or spices before salt.
tracking_metric: Salt shaker off the table today (Y/N).
safety_or_stop_rule: None specific.
notes: WHO tips are verbatim-sourced: limit salt and high-sodium condiments, no salt on the table, limit salty snacks.

what: Steam, bake, grill or boil more often than frying; replace butter/ghee with oils rich in unsaturated fat.
dose: Total fat ≤30% of energy; saturated fat ≤10%; trans fat ≤1% (WHO) — reference values, not daily counting.
why: WHO recommends shifting fat intake away from saturated and trans fats to prevent unhealthy weight gain and NCDs.

sources.title: WHO fact sheet: Healthy diet (updated 26 Jan 2026)
WHO updates guidelines on fats and carbohydrates

cue_suggestion: When planning the cooking method for dinner.
minimum_version: One fried item replaced with a baked/grilled version this week.
normal_version: Most home meals use baking/grilling/steaming; olive or other vegetable oil instead of ghee.
bonus_version: Learn one new oven or air-fryer recipe per week.
joy_pairing: Cook with a family member or while listening to a podcast/IELTS listening practice.
friction_down: Keep a sheet pan and liquid oil at hand; save 5 go-to grill/bake recipes in the app.
friction_up_for_competing: Limit deep-fried takeaway to planned occasions.
if_then_plan: If I'm about to fry, then I will check whether the same food can be baked or grilled.
safety_or_stop_rule: None specific.
notes: Saudi Healthy Food Palm: limit foods high in saturated fatty acids, cholesterol, salt and sugar.

name_en: Protein spread across the day (training days)
name_ar: بروتين موزع على اليوم مع تمارين المقاومة
what: With home resistance training ~4 days/week, include a protein source (eggs, dairy/laban/yoghurt, chicken, fish, legumes) in each main meal; prefer whole foods.
dose: ISSN position stand: 1.4-2.0 g protein/kg body weight/day sufficient for most exercising individuals; ~0.25 g/kg (or 20-40 g) per serving, evenly distributed every 3-4 h. Meta-analysis: intakes above ~1.6 g/kg/day did not further increase resistance-training gains in fat-free mass.
why: Protein intake plus resistance exercise enhances gains in muscle strength and size in healthy adults.

sources.title: A systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression of the effect of protein supplementation on resistance training-induced gains in muscle mass and strength in healthy adults (Br J Sports Med)
International Society of Sports Nutrition Position Stand: protein and exercise (J Int Soc Sports Nutr)

cue_suggestion: When plating each main meal: 'where's the protein?'.
minimum_version: A protein source at breakfast today.
normal_version: A palm-sized protein source at 3 meals on training days.
bonus_version: Plan protein for the week during meal planning (FOOD-08).
joy_pairing: Post-workout snack you enjoy (laban, yoghurt with fruit, eggs) as the immediate reward after the session.
friction_down: Keep boiled eggs/yoghurt/canned tuna or chickpeas ready.
friction_up_for_competing: n/a
if_then_plan: If I finish a workout, then I will have a protein-containing snack or meal within my next eating occasion.
safety_or_stop_rule: Supplements are optional, not required (ISSN: requirements can be met from whole foods). Kidney disease or other medical conditions -> ask a doctor/dietitian before high-protein intake.
notes: ISSN is a sports-nutrition society position stand (some industry-affiliated authors); Morton 2018 is the stronger SR/MA. Don't compute grams daily; use per-meal cue.

what: Once a week, sketch the main meals (at least lunches/dinners) for the coming days.
dose: Not specified by source; start small (plan 3 dinners) and adjust.
why: In a large French adult sample, meal planners had higher diet quality and food variety, and women who planned had lower odds of overweight/obesity (association, not causation).

sources.title: Meal planning is associated with food variety, diet quality and body weight status in a large sample of French adults (IJBNPA)

cue_suggestion: Weekend evening (e.g., Friday after Maghrib) with tea.
minimum_version: Decide tomorrow's lunch and dinner only.
normal_version: Plan 5-7 main meals for the week in the app.
bonus_version: Include one batch-cook session and one new recipe.
joy_pairing: Do it with a favourite drink and a recipe feed/cookbook; let family pick one dish.
friction_down: Reuse a template of 10-15 rotating meals; copy last week's plan and edit.
friction_up_for_competing: Mute food-delivery app notifications.
if_then_plan: If it's Friday evening, then I will open the meal-plan template and fill 3+ dinners.
safety_or_stop_rule: Plan should stay flexible; if planning becomes rigid or anxiety-provoking, simplify.
notes: Pairs with FOOD-09 (grocery list); app can auto-generate the list from the plan.

what: Generate a shopping list from the meal plan and buy from the list.
dose: Not specified by source; 'consistently using a list' was the measured behaviour.
why: Consistent list use was associated with higher diet quality and lower BMI in a cross-sectional study (low-income US adults; association only).

sources.title: Using a Grocery List Is Associated With a Healthier Diet and Lower BMI Among Very High-Risk Adults (J Nutr Educ Behav)

cue_suggestion: Right after finishing the weekly meal plan.
minimum_version: Write the 5 items you need most.
normal_version: Full list grouped by store section, including fruit/veg and whole grains staples.
bonus_version: Keep a standing 'healthy staples' list that auto-adds each week.
joy_pairing: Make the shopping trip a mini-outing (favourite store, new seasonal produce to try).
friction_down: Shared list with family; app auto-builds list from plan.
friction_up_for_competing: Avoid shopping hungry; skip the snack aisle.
if_then_plan: If I go to the store, then I open the list before entering.
safety_or_stop_rule: None specific.
notes: Population differs from her (food-desert residents) — evidence is indirect.

what: Make healthier options visible and easy (fruit bowl, cut veg at front of fridge, water jug) and keep fewer less-healthy options, out of sight; use smaller plates/bowls and single-size packs for treats.
dose: Not specified by source.
why: Cochrane reviews: fewer available options and positioning changes can meaningfully change selection (low-certainty evidence), and people consistently consume more when offered larger portions, packages or tableware.

sources.title: Altering the availability or proximity of food, alcohol, and tobacco products to change their selection and consumption (Cochrane)
Portion, package or tableware size for changing selection and consumption of food, alcohol and tobacco (Cochrane)

cue_suggestion: After unpacking groceries.
minimum_version: Move one healthy food to eye level today.
normal_version: Fruit bowl out; treats in an opaque box; smaller plates by default.
bonus_version: Set up a 'desk snack' drawer with nuts/fruit only.
joy_pairing: Make the fruit bowl/visible shelf pretty — a design project she'll enjoy styling.
friction_down: One-time 20-minute kitchen re-arrangement.
friction_up_for_competing: Buy treats in single-serve sizes; store out of sight.
if_then_plan: If I bring treats home, then they go into the opaque box on the top shelf.
safety_or_stop_rule: None specific.
notes: Most studies were lab-based in high-income countries; certainty low but the actions are low-cost.

what: Eat home-prepared meals most days; learn a small repertoire of quick healthy recipes.
dose: Not specified as a recommendation; the study compared >5 vs <3 home-cooked meals per week.
why: More frequent home-cooked meals were associated with better diet quality (DASH/Mediterranean adherence, more fruit/veg) and lower adiposity in a UK cohort (cross-sectional).

sources.title: Frequency of eating home cooked meals and potential benefits for diet and health: cross-sectional analysis of a population-based cohort study (IJBNPA)

cue_suggestion: After Asr on meal-plan days, start dinner prep.
minimum_version: Assemble a no-cook meal (e.g., yoghurt, bread, salad, eggs) at home.
normal_version: Home-cooked main meal on most days of the week.
bonus_version: Learn one new recipe weekly; batch-cook on the weekend.
joy_pairing: Cook with music/podcast or an IELTS listening episode; cook with family.
friction_down: Prep ingredients in advance; keep 5 quick recipes pinned.
friction_up_for_competing: Remove saved payment in delivery apps or add a 10-minute delay rule.
if_then_plan: If I feel like ordering delivery, then I will first check if a 15-minute pantry meal is possible.
safety_or_stop_rule: Food-safety basics (Saudi palm message on safe purchase/prepare/cook/store).
notes: Saudi Healthy Food Palm: 'Purchase, prepare, cook and store food in ways to ensure food safety'.

name_en: If-then plans for adding healthy foods
what: Write 1-3 specific if-then plans that ADD a healthy food at a set moment (e.g., 'If I have breakfast, then I add a fruit').
dose: Not specified by source.
why: Meta-analysis: implementation intentions effectively promote including healthy foods (d≈0.51), with weaker effects for cutting unhealthy eating (d≈0.29).

sources.title: Do implementation intentions help to eat a healthy diet? A systematic review and meta-analysis of the empirical evidence (Appetite)

cue_suggestion: During weekly meal planning.
minimum_version: One if-then plan for this week.
normal_version: Three plans tied to breakfast, lunch, and afternoon snack.
bonus_version: Review weekly which plans stuck and rewrite the rest.
joy_pairing: Pair the added food with something already enjoyed (fruit with morning coffee).
friction_down: App prompts at the cue time with the plan text.
friction_up_for_competing: n/a
if_then_plan: If it's Sunday meal planning, then I will write one new 'add' plan.
safety_or_stop_rule: Frame plans as additions, not prohibitions.
notes: Supports the app's design: favour 'add' goals over 'ban' goals.

what: Keep roughly consistent meal times each day that fit prayer, study and training; breakfast is optional, not mandatory.
dose: Not specified by source.
why: AHA statement: irregular eating patterns appear less favourable for cardiometabolic health; intentional attention to timing and frequency may help. A BMJ meta-analysis found adding breakfast is not a good weight-loss strategy.

sources.title: Meal Timing and Frequency: Implications for Cardiovascular Disease Prevention: AHA Scientific Statement (Circulation)
Effect of breakfast on weight and energy intake: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials (BMJ)

cue_suggestion: Anchor meals to stable daily events (e.g., after Dhuhr for lunch).
minimum_version: Don't skip lunch today.
normal_version: 2-3 meals at similar times daily; planned snack if needed.
bonus_version: Set meal-time reminders around the study and training schedule.
joy_pairing: Make one meal a day a shared family meal.
friction_down: App reminders at meal anchors; pack lunch for driving lessons/study days.
friction_up_for_competing: n/a
if_then_plan: If I'm out during lunch time, then I'll eat the packed meal instead of skipping.
safety_or_stop_rule: Ramadan and fasting days follow their own schedule; medical conditions (e.g., diabetes) -> follow clinician advice.
notes: AHA statement is expert review; breakfast evidence is low quality/short-term.

what: Eat at least one main meal without phone, laptop or TV; pay attention to the food.
dose: Not specified by source.
why: Meta-analysis: eating while distracted moderately increased immediate intake and increased later intake more; enhancing memory of the meal reduced later intake.

sources.title: Eating attentively: a systematic review and meta-analysis of the effect of food intake memory and awareness on eating (Am J Clin Nutr)

cue_suggestion: When sitting down to lunch/dinner: phone face-down in another spot.
minimum_version: First 5 minutes of the meal screen-free.
normal_version: One full meal per day screen-free.
bonus_version: All main meals screen-free on weekends.
joy_pairing: Make it social: family conversation, or a nice table setting; savour flavours.
friction_down: A phone 'parking spot' away from the table.
friction_up_for_competing: Enable app focus mode at meal times.
if_then_plan: If I sit down to eat, then I put my phone in the parking spot first.
safety_or_stop_rule: None specific.
notes: Also supports digital-wellbeing goals in other clusters.

what: Slow the pace of eating: smaller bites, chew thoroughly, put the fork/bread down between bites.
dose: Not specified by source.
why: Meta-analysis of 22 studies: slower eating rate was associated with lower energy intake than faster eating.

sources.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis examining the effect of eating rate on energy intake and hunger (Am J Clin Nutr)

cue_suggestion: First bite of each main meal.
minimum_version: Put utensils down 3 times during one meal.
normal_version: Aim for an unhurried meal (no rushing to the next task).
bonus_version: Notice fullness midway and decide whether to continue.
joy_pairing: Savouring: name 3 flavours/textures in the meal.
friction_down: Schedule enough time for meals in the day plan.
friction_up_for_competing: Avoid eating while walking or driving.
if_then_plan: If I notice I'm eating fast, then I will pause and drink some water.
safety_or_stop_rule: None specific.
notes: Studies were short-term lab manipulations; long-term effects less certain.

what: If useful, log simple yes/no food habits (fruit/veg portions, sugary drinks, screen-free meal) rather than counting calories.
dose: Not specified by source (the review notes the required 'dose' of self-monitoring is unknown).
why: Systematic review: self-monitoring was consistently associated with weight loss in behavioral programs (weak evidence level); but in college students, calorie-tracker use was associated with more eating concern and dietary restraint.

sources.title: Self-monitoring in weight loss: a systematic review of the literature (J Am Diet Assoc)
Calorie counting and fitness tracking technology: Associations with eating disorder symptomatology (Eat Behav)

cue_suggestion: Evening wind-down, 1-minute check-in.
minimum_version: One tap: 'ate fruit/veg today?'.
normal_version: 3 habit checkboxes per day.
bonus_version: Weekly 5-minute review of patterns, not numbers.
joy_pairing: Visual streak or garden-style progress, not numbers or scores about the body.
friction_down: One-tap checkboxes inside the life-OS app.
friction_up_for_competing: Don't install calorie-counting apps by default.
if_then_plan: If tracking starts to feel stressful or I skip meals to 'score', then I stop tracking for 2 weeks and use habits only.
safety_or_stop_rule: STOP RULE: stop tracking if it causes anxiety, guilt, preoccupation with food/weight, skipping meals, or compensatory exercise; speak with a doctor or qualified professional if these persist. No calorie counting, no weight-based targets by default.
notes: Burke review population mostly white women in weight-loss programs; she is not in a weight-loss program, so apply lightly.

what: Record period start date, number of bleeding days, heaviness, and symptoms (cramps, headaches, mood, bloating) that affect daily activities.
dose: Not specified; record each cycle. Reference: normal cycle 24-38 days (OWH).
why: OWH advises keeping a record to understand what is normal for you and to share with a healthcare provider.

sources.title: US Office on Women's Health: Your menstrual cycle (page accessed 2026-09-28; year = access year)

cue_suggestion: On the first day of the period, and a one-tap symptom note on heavy/painful days.
minimum_version: Log start date only.
normal_version: Start/end dates + heaviness + main symptoms.
bonus_version: Note energy levels to adapt training and study load.
joy_pairing: Pair with a comfort ritual (warm drink, lighter plan) on day 1.
friction_down: One-tap log in the app; auto-reminder when a period is expected.
friction_up_for_competing: n/a
if_then_plan: If my period starts, then I log it immediately in the app.
safety_or_stop_rule: See a doctor (OWH) if cycles are shorter than 24 or longer than 38 days, bleeding soaks a pad every 1-2 hours, clots larger than a quarter, bleeding lasts more than 8 days, or pain/bleeding disrupts daily life.
notes: Health data is sensitive: keep cycle data local/encrypted in the app with explicit consent. No prediction of fertility or diagnosis.

name_ar: أطعمة غنية بالحديد مع فيتامين C
what: Include iron sources regularly (red meat, poultry, fish; lentils, beans, spinach, fortified cereals) and pair plant sources with vitamin C foods (citrus, tomatoes, peppers, strawberries, broccoli).
dose: Women 19-50: 18 mg iron/day (NIH ODS RDA).
why: Women with heavy periods are at higher risk of insufficient iron; vitamin C and meat/fish improve absorption of plant iron (NIH ODS).

sources.title: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements: Iron fact sheet for consumers (page accessed 2026-09-28; year = access year)

cue_suggestion: During weekly meal planning: tag 3+ iron-rich meals.
minimum_version: Add lemon/tomato to a lentil or bean dish.
normal_version: Iron-rich food in most days' main meal.
bonus_version: Plan extra iron-rich meals around period week.
joy_pairing: Favourite dishes: adas with lemon, kabsa with salad, liver/meat dishes if liked.
friction_down: Keep canned lentils/beans and frozen spinach stocked.
friction_up_for_competing: n/a
if_then_plan: If I cook lentils or beans, then I add lemon or tomato.
safety_or_stop_rule: Do not start iron supplements without a doctor and blood test; keep supplements away from children (accidental iron overdose is a leading cause of fatal poisoning in children under 6). Heavy periods or fatigue -> see a doctor.
notes: US source (NIH ODS) used because no Saudi-specific iron page was verified.

name_ar: نمط حياة لمتلازمة تكيس المبايض (عند التشخيص فقط)
what: Only if a doctor has diagnosed PCOS: follow a healthy lifestyle combining physical activity, a healthy eating pattern consistent with population guidelines, and behavioural strategies, coordinated with her clinician.
dose: Guideline (adults): 150-300 min/week moderate or 75-150 min/week vigorous aerobic activity, plus muscle-strengthening on 2 non-consecutive days/week; limit sedentary time. No specific diet composition is preferred.
why: The 2023 international guideline recommends lifestyle intervention for all women with PCOS and states there are benefits of a healthy lifestyle even without weight loss.

sources.title: Recommendations from the 2023 international evidence-based guideline for the assessment and management of polycystic ovary syndrome (Eur J Endocrinol)
Recommendations From the 2023 International Evidence-based Guideline for the Assessment and Management of PCOS (JCEM full text)

cue_suggestion: Same cues as BODY-cluster exercise and FOOD-cluster eating habits.
minimum_version: Keep the general healthy-eating and activity habits in this library.
normal_version: Activity volume per guideline + healthy eating habits; regular follow-up with clinician.
bonus_version: Ask the clinician about referral to a dietitian.
joy_pairing: Choose activities she enjoys; the guideline emphasises individual preferences.
friction_down: Reuse existing app routines; no separate PCOS diet needed.
friction_up_for_competing: n/a
if_then_plan: If I receive a PCOS diagnosis, then I will ask my doctor which of these actions to prioritise.
safety_or_stop_rule: No self-diagnosis. Irregular cycles, excess hair growth, or acne -> see a doctor for assessment. Avoid restrictive diets; guideline highlights weight stigma awareness.
notes: Conditional: no evidence she has PCOS; hide by default in the app unless she enables it.

what: Apply broad-spectrum, water-resistant sunscreen to all skin not covered by clothing before going outside; reapply when outdoors.
dose: SPF 30 or higher; reapply every 2 hours and after sweating/toweling (AAD).
why: AAD recommends sunscreen as part of sun protection against skin cancer and sun damage.

sources.title: AAD: How to select a sunscreen / understand sunscreen labels (page accessed 2026-09-28; year = access year)

cue_suggestion: After the morning face wash, before moisturizer/makeup — or at the door with keys.
minimum_version: Face and hands before any outdoor time.
normal_version: Every morning on exposed skin + reapply on long outdoor days (driving lessons, walks).
bonus_version: Keep a second sunscreen in the bag/car for reapplication.
joy_pairing: Choose a texture/scent she genuinely likes; make it part of a pleasant morning skincare ritual.
friction_down: Sunscreen placed next to the toothbrush and one in the car.
friction_up_for_competing: n/a
if_then_plan: If I pick up my car keys/bag, then I check sunscreen is on.
safety_or_stop_rule: Stop a product causing rash/irritation. New or changing moles/spots -> see a dermatologist.
notes: Jeddah/Makkah sun exposure makes this high-value; also relevant during outdoor walks and driving practice.

what: Wash face with a gentle, non-abrasive, alcohol-free cleanser and lukewarm water using fingertips; don't scrub; pat dry; moisturize if skin is dry or itchy.
dose: Limit washing to twice a day and after sweating (AAD).
why: AAD advises gentle cleansing because scrubbing and harsh products irritate skin.

sources.title: AAD: Face washing 101 (page accessed 2026-09-28; year = access year)

cue_suggestion: Morning after wudu/brushing teeth; night before bed; after workouts.
minimum_version: Night cleanse only.
normal_version: Morning + night cleanse, plus after exercise; moisturizer if dry.
bonus_version: Review products quarterly; remove ones that sting or irritate.
joy_pairing: Treat the night routine as a calming wind-down signal (dim light, favourite scent).
friction_down: Keep cleanser + moisturizer + sunscreen together as a 3-step kit.
friction_up_for_competing: n/a
if_then_plan: If I finish a workout, then I wash my face before anything else.
safety_or_stop_rule: Persistent acne, rash, or skin changes -> consult a board-certified dermatologist (AAD).
notes: AAD is a professional body; recommendations are expert guidance rather than trial-graded.

what: Shampoo the scalp (not full length) as often as hair gets oily; condition after washing; detangle wet hair with a wide-tooth comb; blot with a towel; limit heat styling, use low/medium heat and heat protectant.
dose: Frequency depends on hair type: oily straight hair may be daily; dry/textured hair at least every 2-3 weeks as needed (AAD).
why: AAD dermatologists advise these steps to keep hair healthy and avoid damage.

sources.title: AAD: Tips for healthy hair (page accessed 2026-09-28; year = access year)
AAD: Hair loss - signs and symptoms (page accessed 2026-09-28; year = access year)

cue_suggestion: Wash-day routine (fixed weekday evening).
minimum_version: Use a wide-tooth comb on wet hair.
normal_version: Scalp-focused shampoo + conditioner; air-dry when possible.
bonus_version: Heat-free styling on most days.
joy_pairing: Wash-day as self-care evening (podcast, favourite products).
friction_down: Keep wide-tooth comb and heat protectant in the bathroom.
friction_up_for_competing: Store flat iron/curler in a cupboard, not on the counter.
if_then_plan: If I use a hot tool, then I apply heat protectant and use low/medium setting.
safety_or_stop_rule: See a board-certified dermatologist for hair loss: gradual thinning, widening part, thinner ponytail, sudden bald patches, clumps falling out, or itching/burning/tenderness of the scalp (AAD). No self-treatment of hair loss.
notes: Hair-loss referral signs come from the AAD 'signs and symptoms' page.

name_en: Brush twice daily + clean between teeth
name_ar: تفريش الأسنان مرتين وتنظيف ما بينها
what: Brush with fluoride toothpaste twice a day for two minutes; clean between teeth daily (floss, interdental brushes, or water flosser — whichever she'll use).
dose: Twice daily, 2 minutes, fluoride toothpaste; interdental cleaning daily (ADA).
why: ADA: fluoride toothpaste prevents tooth decay; Saudi preventive guideline cites good evidence that brushing and flossing prevent gingivitis.

cue_suggestion: After breakfast and as the last step before bed.

normal_version: Morning + night brushing; interdental cleaning at night.
bonus_version: Dental visit booked per dentist's recommended interval.
joy_pairing: 2-minute song or a 2-minute IELTS vocabulary audio while brushing.
friction_down: Floss picks next to the toothbrush; travel kit in bag.
friction_up_for_competing: n/a

safety_or_stop_rule: Bleeding gums that persist, tooth pain, or sensitivity -> see a dentist.
notes: ADA: see your dentist regularly, frequency tailored to individual risk.

what: Book a primary-care preventive visit and follow the Saudi Clinical Preventive Guideline checklist for adults 18-59 as the clinician applies it: blood pressure, BMI and waist, dental/mouth exam, and cervical screening when eligible per the guideline's criteria.
dose: Per Saudi guideline: BP screening for adults ≥18 — every 3-5 years if 18-39, not at increased risk and prior normal reading; annually if at increased risk. BMI & waist every 2 years. Cervical screening: guideline cites USPSTF criteria for women aged 21-65 (clinician determines eligibility and interval). Blood sugar: from age 35 every 3 years, earlier if overweight with risk factors.
why: The national preventive guideline sets these as the recommended clinical preventive services for adults.

cue_suggestion: Birthday month: annual 'health admin' review.
minimum_version: Check the date of your last blood pressure reading.
normal_version: Annual review in the app; book whatever is due.
bonus_version: Keep results (BP, etc.) in a private health note to share with the doctor.
joy_pairing: Combine with a treat outing after the appointment.
friction_down: App stores due dates and pre-fills a booking reminder (e.g., via Sehhaty).
friction_up_for_competing: n/a
if_then_plan: If it's my birthday month, then I review which checks are due and book them.
safety_or_stop_rule: No self-diagnosis; any symptoms go to a doctor without waiting for the routine schedule. Folic acid 0.4-0.8 mg daily is recommended by the guideline only for women planning or capable of pregnancy — discuss with a doctor if relevant.
notes: Source: Saudi Clinical Preventive Guideline 3rd ed. 2023 (Public Health Authority). Sehhaty mention is an app suggestion, not from the source.

what: Keep vaccinations current per the Saudi adult schedule: annual influenza; Tdap once then Td booster every 10 years; ask a doctor about catch-up vaccines (e.g., HPV, MMR, varicella, hepatitis B) based on her records.
dose: Influenza: 1 dose annually. Tdap once, then Td booster every 10 years. HPV: 3-dose catch-up for females aged 15-26 (per the guideline's table). Others only if no evidence of immunity.
why: The Saudi Clinical Preventive Guideline's adult vaccination table lists these as recommended immunizations for adults 18+.
